newsitem.title: USA: Gasoline imports seen having modest market impact.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline imports seen having modest market impact.

text.p: The wave of gasoline imports expected to reach New York Harbor (NYH) in coming days should have only a muted effect on prices, traders said, in the wake of the recent sharp declines and the fire at a Tosco's huge East Coast refinery.
Traders said arb trading last week assured the market of a flood of European gasoline for the next few weeks, as U.S. players sought to build their low inventory levels.
In addition, a number of gasoline cargoes from Europe and the Caribbean are expected to arrive in New York Harbor (NYH) in the coming days, which prevented a significant bullish move.
"Imports have been relatively high, especially for this time of the year," said Tom Knight, trader with Fina. "But buyers have be been pretty coy since the market started to break down," he added.
One 500,000-barrel cargo of gasoline is set to arrive in NYH December 17, with an up to another million barrels may reach port by the end of the month.

Other players said expectations for increased gasoline supplies helped push prices lower during recent trading. Cash prices for reformulated (A5) gasoline in New York Harbor was at about 73.50 cents a gallon on Friday and was down to about 65.75 cents late Thursday.
"The market's (at current levels) because everybody knew about the imports. It's probably over-discounted them if anything," said a trader with a major oil company in Connecticut.
A fire Wednesday evening shut Tosco's 140,000 barrel per day fluid catalytic cracker at its Linden, New Jersey refinery. No estimates on how long the unit would be out of service were available.
